newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam minister says 1997 growth target 9-10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam minister says 1997 growth target 9-10 pct.

text.p: Vietnam is targeting economic growth of nine to 10 percent in 1997 after two consecutive years of 9.5-percent growth, Minister for Planning and Investment Tran Xuan Gia said in an interview published on Monday.
Gia told the weekly Vietnam Investment Review that the government was also aiming for industrial production growth of 14-14.5 percent and agricultural output growth of 4.6-4.9 percent.
He said the economy performed well last year despite natural disasters, with gross domestic product (GDP) up 9.5 percent, industrial output up 14.1 percent and exports up 35 percent.

"At the same time, in 1996, there appeared problems that cannot be neglected," he said. "We imported more than we exported. That might lead to bad consequences if the situation is not overcome in time."
Vietnam's trade deficit ballooned to a record $4 billion last year, equivalent to about 18 percent of GDP, from $2.1 billion in 1995.

Gia singled out infrastructure, energy, agriculture and raw material-based industries as the key areas for government spending this year and said that although the state sector would keep its "leading role", other sectors would also be encouraged.

"State-owned economic components will still play the leading role but they do not necessarily need to account for a high percentage," he said. "It is important that this...component maintains key economic branches with high economic efficiency."
The ruling Communist Party affirmed at a policy-defining congress six months ago that the state sector would remain the country's economic driving force.
However, a proposal to increase the state sector's share of GDP to 60 percent from around 40 percent was dropped from the conclave's final policy document.
